MeS3 $111,870 to $125,306 p.a.+ Superannuation & Salary Sacrifice Benefits

SA, Adelaide 5000

Full Time, Permanent Role Available 

About the role

Join SA Pathology as the Haemostasis Scientific Manager and lead a high-performing team delivering specialist diagnostic services within the Royal Adelaide Hospital Core Laboratory. You'll provide operational leadership across the Haemostasis and thrombotic section, managing scientific and technical activities while ensuring high-quality, timely and patient-focused laboratory services. Working closely with Haemostasis Principal Scientist and clinical leads, you'll oversee daily operations, set priorities and drive service excellence across the discipline.

This is an outstanding opportunity to shape the future of a specialist laboratory service through leadership, innovation and continuous improvement. You'll mentor and develop scientific and technical staff, optimise workflows, implement new techniques and quality initiatives, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to maintain the highest standards of clinical governance, safety and diagnostic practice.

About You

You are an experienced Medical Scientist and inspiring leader who is passionate about delivering exceptional diagnostic services and developing high-performing teams.

- Bachelor of Science or Medical Laboratory Science (or equivalent)
- Extensive diagnostic pathology and laboratory leadership experience
- Expertise in quality systems, workflow management and staff development
- Strong communication, problem-solving and stakeholder engagement skills

About us

Statewide Clinical Support Services (SCSS) is a unique public healthcare organisation that serves health consumers and provides specialist clinical services to the health system in South Australia. SCSS encompasses BreastScreen SA, SA Dental, SA Medical Imaging, SA Pathology, and SA Pharmacy. Come and work with us to improve the health and well-being of South Australians, across all age groups and at any time of their life or health need. 

What we offer

Salary Benefits: Enjoy flexible salary packaging options, including up to $9,010 each FBT year for living expenses (such as mortgage, rent, utilities and groceries) plus an additional $2,650 for meal and entertainment expenses.

Professional Development: Opportunity to apply for reimbursement of eligible professional development activities, and access to dedicated leave for ongoing learning.

Annual Leave: Enjoy paid recreation leave for essential rejuvenation, with leave loading applied.

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program for you and your family, plus an annual voluntary flu vaccination to support your wellbeing.

Employee Assistance Program: Confidential counselling and support services for you and your family via our Employee Assistance Program.

Diversity and inclusion:

Statewide supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are encouraged to apply. 

Application Information:

Please refer to the role description for essential educational-vocational qualifications that may be required.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and compliant Immunisation screening as indicated in the role description.

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Please note that unsolicited applications from recruitment agencies or third parties will not be accepted for this position.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your Role as Head of Asset Performance

This role operates across both strategy and operations, ensuring that asset performance insights directly influence organisational strategy while driving improvements in how assets are utilised, maintained, and optimised. This role oversees the daily operations of the Asset Performance Department, with responsibility for ensuring strategic goals are met by setting operational policies, maintaining budgets and managing and developing employees. The role focuses on understanding asset behaviour, performance trends, and lifecycle outcomes - including the development and alignment of maintenance planning approaches - to enhance reliability, efficiency, and overall value.

You'll deliver this role by:

Provide strategic and operational advice to optimise asset performance and inform investment, maintenance and lifecycle decisions.

Contribute to the development and refinement of the organisation's Value & Asset Management Strategy by providing evidence-based insights on asset performance, risks, and opportunities.

Provide forward-looking analysis on asset condition, lifecycle requirements, and investment needs to inform capital planning and prioritisation.

Establish and monitor key performance indicators to identify trends, performance gaps or emerging risks.

Oversee the planning and coordination of asset lifecycle projects (e.g. RTOs, renewals, replacements, upgrades), ensuring alignment with asset performance objectives and organisational priorities.

Coordinate the planning and delivery of lifecycle activities to achieve agreed outcomes and minimise disruption to customers, services, and business operations.

Monitor delivery of lifecycle initiatives to ensure quality outcomes, minimal operational impact, and alignment to agreed objectives.

Integrate preventive, predictive, and condition-based maintenance practices to optimise asset reliability and minimise unplanned downtime.

Manage medium and long-term maintenance schedules to support lifecycle optimisation and capital planning inputs.

Identify opportunities to refine maintenance strategies based on performance data, failure analysis, and operational feedback.

Work closely with operational teams to optimise how assets are utilised, maintained, and managed to improve reliability, availability, and cost efficiency.

Promote the adoption of proactive and predictive approaches to maintenance, reducing reactive work and unplanned disruptions.

Embed structured problem-solving approaches to address recurring asset performance issues and operational challenges.

Drive alignment between maintenance planning, asset performance objectives, and operational delivery practices.

What We Offer

Attractive Remuneration plus packaging benefits - Boost your take-home pay by up to $18,550 annually through not-for-profit tax concessions

Work-life balance - Enjoy flexible hours that work around your life, we promote a culture that values personal time and well-being

What We're Looking For

Significant experience in asset management, asset performance, infrastructure, or similar operational environments, including demonstrated experience in asset lifecycle management.

Bachelor Degree in Engineering, Asset Management, Infrastructure Management, or a related discipline.

Experience using asset systems, analytics and performance tools to evaluate asset performance and drive operational and strategic improvements.

Proven experience working across both strategic planning and operational delivery contexts, including maintenance planning approaches (preventive, predictive, condition-based).

Demonstrated experience contributing to or supporting capital planning, lifecycle investment decisions, or asset-related business cases.

Knowledge of risk-based asset management, including criticality assessment and failure analysis.

Certification or training aligned asset management frameworks (eg. ISO 55000, IAM).

Proven leadership capability with strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.

Excellent communication, negotiation, and influencing skills.

A Valuable Addition, Yet Not a Must-Have!

Experience in aged care, retirement living, disability services, or health-community infrastructure.

Experience managing external contractors, facilities management providers, or outsourced maintenance models.

Experience leading asset management transformation, system uplift, or cultural shifts toward proactive maintenance

Essential Requirements

Proof of COVID-19 vaccination status (or as required by legislation and WMQ policy)

Relevant probity checks required by legislation and WMQ Limited policy.

Current Driver's Licence and willingness to travel for work

result.description:
Kununurra, Full Time, Hospitality
Vacancy Listing Dates 24/07/2026 to 21/08/2026
Please Quote Reference Number 17483
- Skilled Hotel/Motel Manager, Landscape Gardener, and Handyperson wanted
- Full time roles
- Opportunities with The Kimberley Grande Resort

Kimberley Grande Resort in Kununurra have the following vacancies on offer:
- Hotel/Motel Manager
- Landscape Gardener
- Handyperson

Hotel/Motel Manager

The manager will assume responsibility for overseeing day-to-day operations, ensuring guest satisfaction, directing staff, and maintaining profitability. The multifaceted responsibilities of this position demand business acumen, exceptional interpersonal skills, exceptional problem-solving skills and a genuine passion for guest service.

We are seeking a Hotel/Motel Manager to:
- Manage hotel services - accommodation and food and beverage.
- Oversee events and conferences.
- Manage corporate bookings and enquiries.
- Human resource management.
- Troubleshoot any issues arising in hotel operations.
- Liaise with contractors and suppliers.
- Supervise any maintenance work and renovations.
- Safeguard security and compliance, conducting inspections where necessary.
- Manage heads of departments or entire teams including supervision of ordering stock
- Drive forward sales strategies and oversee expenditure
- Handle financial responsibilities by ensuring high occupancy levels,
- Manage budgets and controlling expenditures.
- Track hotel revenues, setting sales targets and optimise profits.
- Analyse sales figures, reports and the different market segments and channels to define the best-suited pricing and distribution strategies.
- Maintain statistical and financial records.
- Monitor and motivate staff with constructive communication in a positive work environment and a shared vision of targets and career progression.

Skills and Qualifications:
- Diploma or degree in hospitality management or a related field.
- Two to five years of experience in a supervisory or management capacity within the hospitality industry.
- Exceptional leadership, interpersonal, and organisational abilities.
- Ability to lead people not just manage them.
- Proficiency in computer applications and hospitality management systems (RMS is preferable or similar).
- Willingness to work variable shifts, including weekends and holidays.
- Possess a police check or the ability to complete the check.

Landscape Gardener

We are also seeking a Landscape Gardener to join our team, applicants must have at least 2-3 years' experience in a similar role.

Duties include:
- Preparing and maintaining seedbeds and growing sites
- Propagating and planting trees, bushes, hedges, flowers and bulbs
- Preparing lawn areas by spreading top soil and planting grass, and by laying instant turf
- Maintaining planted and grassed areas by weeding, trimming, fertilising, watering and mowing
- Ensuring the grounds are clean for guests
- Pruning trees and hedges, and installing plant support and protection devices
- Preparing plans and drawings, selecting materials and plants, and scheduling landscape construction
- Setting out and installing hardscape and softscape structures
- Constructing gravel and paved areas, walls, fences, pergolas, ponds, barbecues and garden furniture
- Examining trees to assess their condition and determine treatment
- Lopping limbs off trees and shaping branches using chain and handsaws
- Spraying and dusting plants and trees to control insects and disease, and felling diseased trees

Handyperson

In addition, we require a Handyperson to join our team full time as well.

You will be responsible for:
- General repairs around the property and rooms.
- Plumbing repairs including Unblocking sinks, fixing leaky taps, and replacing tap washers.
- Simple electrical repairs
- Painting and carpentry repairs to ensure the rooms and grounds are in good condition
- Outdoor maintenance such as clearing gutters, fixing fences, mowing lawns, and general yard upkeep.

Applicants must have:
- At least 1 year of experience in a similar role
- Proficiency in using hand and power tools.
- Basic working knowledge of carpentry, plumbing, and electrical systems
- Ability to perform manual labour, including lifting heavy objects and standing for long periods.
- Strong communication skills 
- A valid driver's licence and relevant construction induction training (e.g., White Card in Australia)

The successful applicants will receive a remuneration between $70,000 - $100,000.

If you are ready to take your career to the next level in a challenging, busy yet rewarding position, this may be the perfect opportunity for you.

Apply now! -
https://www.netyourjob.com.au/jobs/17483.php

Sponsorship may be available to the right person.

This established medical practice in the Cessnock area offers a professional and modern environment designed to provide high-quality care to the local community. The facility is equipped with contemporary treatment rooms and diagnostic technology, supporting a clinical setting that balances emergency care capabilities with routine primary health. Operating as a  mixed-billing practice , the clinic ensures a diverse patient demographic, providing a stimulating clinical environment for nursing staff. The successful candidate will work within a collaborative team composition of dedicated General Practitioners and fellow nursing professionals, all supported by a high-functioning administrative team. 

 A significant focus is placed on comprehensive patient care, with extensive  CDM support  and dedicated systems for immunizations and wound management already in place. Nurses are encouraged to exercise a high degree of  clinical autonomy , taking ownership of patient outcomes while benefiting from a structured support network. For those looking to expand their professional horizons, the practice offers  special interest opportunities  in areas such as well-women’s screening and preventative health. Furthermore, the clinic is committed to the professional evolution of its staff, providing  CPD support  and clear pathways for those interested in  supervisor opportunities  to mentor junior staff or students. 

 The role is designed to accommodate a healthy work-life balance through  flexible working arrangements , including part-time or casual options, though a willingness to contribute to a shared weekend roster is valued. Beyond the clinic walls, the Cessnock and Hunter region offers exceptional  lifestyle benefits , ranging from world-class vineyards and a renowned culinary scene to affordable housing and stunning natural landscapes. This position represents an ideal career move for a nurse seeking a positive team culture in a location that offers both professional fulfillment and a relaxed, high-quality lifestyle.   Apply Now
